questions.title: How does the browser render a web page?
questions.answer: Browsers parse HTML and CSS, construct the relevant document and style structures, calculate layout, paint visual content and composite the resulting layers for display.
questions.underTheHood: Rendering work depends on document structure, computed styles and layout requirements. Browsers may optimize or skip some stages for particular changes.
pitfalls: Not every style change triggers layout.
Repeated layout reads and writes can cause layout thrashing.
Long JavaScript tasks can delay rendering.

questions.title: What is requestAnimationFrame()?
questions.answer: requestAnimationFrame() schedules a callback before an upcoming browser repaint. It is commonly used for visual animations.
questions.underTheHood: The browser invokes animation-frame callbacks as part of its rendering update process when appropriate.
pitfalls: Animation frame timing depends on the display and browser scheduling.
Callbacks may be paused in background tabs.
followUps: How does requestAnimationFrame differ from setTimeout?
